title: Ending curbside Christmas tree collection
subtitle: Also: Cambridge river crossings, Victoria Street expropriation, transit priority lanes, a Cambridge tax increment grant and surplus land.
overview: The committee recommended ending the Region's curbside Christmas tree collection after January 2026 service, replacing it from January 2027 with a fundraiser pickup run with the Family and Children's Services Foundation {{vote:m7}}. Staff said the service costs $540,000 a year and participation has fallen. Residents would also get free drop-off at Regional waste sites for two weeks each January, or could set trees out on monthly bulk item day.

The committee also recommended expropriating part of a property at 247 Duke Street West for Victoria Street North road improvements {{vote:m6}}. It directed staff to assess Grand and Speed River crossings in Cambridge as part of long-term transportation planning {{vote:m8}}. On the consent agenda, it recommended new bus-priority lane designations in Kitchener, Cambridge and Woolwich, a tax increment grant for 30 George Street South in Cambridge, and transferring surplus land at 110 Howard Avenue to Woolwich.
These are committee recommendations and go to Regional Council for a final decision. Staff said more detail on the tree program logistics could come to Council in October.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended ending Regional curbside tree collection in January 2027, partnering with the Family and Children's Services Foundation on a fundraiser pickup, offering two weeks of free drop-off each January, and amending the Emterra contract {{vote:m7}}.
The committee recommended expropriating a partial strip of land at 247 Duke Street West in Kitchener for road improvements between King and Weber Streets {{vote:m6}}.
The committee directed staff to assess whether Grand and Speed River crossings can handle growth to 2051, consider new vehicle, pedestrian and cycling crossings, and report back {{vote:m8}}.
The committee recommended amending the Traffic and Parking By-law to add bus turn exceptions and bus-only lanes at locations in Kitchener, Cambridge and Woolwich.
The committee recommended a joint Tax Increment Grant of up to $173,080 for the Cambridge property, financed from incremental tax revenue after redevelopment.
The committee recommended declaring the Woolwich lands surplus and authorizing their transfer to the Township of Woolwich for nominal consideration.

debate: Supporters of the tree change cited cost savings, low participation, and a chance to support a local charity. They pointed to a similar program in Guelph as the model.

Several councillors raised communication concerns: residents may not know about the change. Staff promised a broad campaign, including possibly the printed collection calendar, and said logistics and donation amounts are still being worked out.

One councillor asked whether the procurement could be treated as a trial so the service could return. Staff said it would. Another asked about the Foundation's capacity, and staff expressed confidence given its volunteers.

Opponents said low participation as a test could be applied to other programs, that the optics of removing a service while taxes rise are poor, and that the change makes disposal harder for families and weakens a tradition. One also asked how the Foundation would use the funds.

On river crossings, supporters cited congestion on Cambridge's few bridges and suggested pedestrian bridges, such as near a Cambridge high school and the hospital. Staff said the work would fit into the Integrated Mobility Plan.
